steps: Open the annual stack with File → Open: LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif, a band per year, yr1985 to yr2024.
Click the map on the cleared forest to drop a pin: the pixel the chart and the table follow.
Open Tools → Change detection → LandTrendr and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series. The parameters are the defaults.
Read the vertices and segments on the chart and the mapped event in the Statistics table.
Open the annual stack of the LandTrendr guide with File → Open: LT_Stack_NDVI_Rondonia.tif.
Drop pin 1 on pixel 306, 913.
Open Tools → Change detection → BEAST (Bayesian changepoints) and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series; the parameters are the defaults.
The chart draws the model and the probability of a changepoint in each year.

Open the folder of the 125 Landsat dates with File → Open folder.... In the Display panel choose NIR as the band and red for the normalized difference, so the chart shows the NDVI; the quality band is found by its name.
Drop a pin on the forest cleared in May–June 2022.
Open Tools → Change detection → CCDC and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series. The parameters are the defaults.
The chart draws the segments, and the Statistics table their breaks and magnitudes.
Open the same folder of Landsat dates (File → Open folder...), NIR as the band and red for the normalized difference.
Drop a pin on the forest cleared in May–June 2022.
Open Tools → Change detection → CODED (degradation), set Monitoring starts to 2022 and Training years to 2, and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series.
The chart draws the NDFI and the changes CODED finds on it.

Open the folder of the 125 Landsat dates with File → Open folder...: NIR as the band and red for the normalized difference. With the QA_PIXEL band in the files, choose it as the Quality band (Janus finds it by its name).
Drop a pin on pixel 378, 778, the second pixel of the guide: about 11 km north-west of pin 1.
Open Tools → Change detection → S-CCD (stochastic CCDC) and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series. The parameters are the defaults.
The chart draws the model that S-CCD updates with each image, and the Statistics table the state of the pixel at the last date.
Open the MODIS EVI stack with File → Open: one GeoTIFF with a band per date, named EVI_2001_01_01 and so on.
Drop a pin on pixel 435, 153, a field with EVI of about 0.42 a year until 2012 and about 0.3 since.
Open Tools → Change detection → BFAST and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series. The parameters are the defaults.
The chart draws the trend and the season with their breaks; the Statistics table lists them.
With the EVI stack open and the pin on pixel 435, 153, open Tools → Change detection → BFAST Lite.
Tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series; the parameters are the defaults.
The chart draws the trend and the breaks of the single model BFAST Lite fits.
With the EVI stack open and the pin on pixel 435, 153, open Tools → Change detection → BFAST Monitor.
Set Monitoring starts to 2010 and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series.
The chart draws the stable history before 2010 and the monitoring period after it, with the break BFAST Monitor finds.
Open the MODIS EVI stack of the BFAST guide with File → Open.
Drop a pin on pixel 71, 319, a field with a strong season every year.
Open Tools → Temporal dynamics → Phenology and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series. The parameters are the defaults.
The chart draws the smoothed curve and the seasons; the Statistics table gives their start, peak and end.
Open the 41 annual composites with File → Open folder... (landsat_medoid_1985 to landsat_medoid_2025, with 0 declared as no data).
Drop a pin near the river, on pixel 1426, 1199.
Open Tools → Temporal dynamics → AR(1) trend and tick Fit the cursor, pins and ROI series. The window stays at its defaults.
The chart draws the AR(1) line next to the OLS one, and the Statistics table gives the slope, its standard error and ρ.
